title: Cost optimization automation: batching/caching defaults, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Patel
commit_summaries: Add autotune engine for batching and cache defaults (core/runtime)
Introduce quantization profile registry and selection heuristics
Unit-econ CLI + backend: cost simulation and per-route recommendation UI hooks
Update default config schema and docs, add integration tests
Fix flake in batcher unit test discovered by CI
description:
Motivation: Many customers run into suboptimal unit economics because per-route defaults (batching window, cache TTL, quantization point) are conservative and require manual tuning. This PR introduces an automated defaults/autotune pipeline that picks batching and caching defaults based on traffic profiles, a quantization profile registry with heuristics for model families + sequence length distributions, and a unit-economics (uecon) tooling surface (CLI + backend + UI hooks) to simulate and recommend config changes.

Summary of changes: Adds an autotune engine in core/runtime that ingests recent request histograms and suggests per-route defaults (target latency SLO + budget) and a feedback loop to validate changes in staging. Implements a small quantization profile registry that maps model families and common sequence length percentiles to a recommended quant (INT8/FP16/mixed) with fallback rules; profiles are versioned and can be pinned per-deployment. Adds a uecon CLI that runs offline simulations given token distributions, model cost curves, and config deltas; the backend exposes an API used by a new recommendations component in the console UI. Updates defaults.yaml schema and docs. Includes unit/integration tests and CI updates.

Notable technical details: - Autotune engine uses a combination of histogram aggregation (per-route), cost model lookup (GPU kernel cost curves), and a simple hill-climb search that respects SLO constraints. Changes are suggested as "soft defaults" which can be applied as canary rules first. - Batching improvements: allow dynamic max_batch based on 95th percentile of concurrent requests and introduce a per-route batching window cap to preserve latency SLOs. - KV/prefix caching default TTLs are inferred from observed request entropy (low entropy -> longer TTL). - Quant profiles: profiles are small JSON-ish entries (kept in core/inference/quant_profiles.py) with compatibility tags (model family, seq_len_range, supported_kernels). The selection heuristic prefers highest quant that passes a small synthetic quality budget check (approx eval with cached prompts). - Unit-econ tooling: accepts inputs (token distribution, route qps, model id, billing rates, hardware cost) and outputs estimated per-1M-token cost, recommended changes (batching, cache TTL, quant), and expected cost delta + risk band.

release_notes: Add automated defaults/autotune for batching and caching, quantization profile registry with selection heuristics, and unit-economics tooling (CLI + backend + Console UI hooks). Feature gated; opt-in rollout recommended.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated under feature.cost_opt.autotune; enable in staging first. Alerts added: autotune.suggested_changes.rate, uecon.simulation.failures. Watch p95 latency, error rates, and model-serving OOMs during canary.
human_readable_summary: Merged PR that implements autotune defaults for batching/caching, quantization profile registry, and unit-economics tooling to recommend cost-saving config changes. Ship behind feature flag and canary before full rollout.
